title: Di'ibil al-Khuza'i with the Lady and Muslim bin al-Walid
logline: A poet charms a quick-witted lady with verses and takes her to his friend's fine house; the friend sends him to market with a kerchief, and when he returns with the feast he finds the door shut on him.
moral: Cleverness with words is no defence against a cleverer friend: be careful whose house, whose money and whose errand you are on.
tone: Light comedy of manners that turns into a farce at a closed door; witty, never crude. The woman is the quickest mind in the film; the joke is on Diibil.

beats.summary: Diibil, idle by a door in Baghdad, sees a beautiful woman pass.
He addresses her with a verse of sleeplessness and tears (first verse ribbon).
She answers at once in the same metre and sense.
Her second answer loops round his head and crowns him with his own heart.
He changes metre to test her; she changes with him without a pause. 3 for 3.
She agrees to go with him.
His own room is not fit for a guest (thought cloud with a mouse).
Muslim welcomes them to his fine house; his eye rests on the lady.
The host has no money for food.
Muslim gives Diibil a precious kerchief to sell: the errand that removes him.
Kerchief sold, food and drink bought.
The room is empty; the private door slams shut.
An arm takes the food; Muslim thanks him mockingly and shuts him out.
Diibil understands he was sent away on purpose.
Duel of stinging verses through the door; Diibil kicks it and hurts his foot.
Muslim: my house, my kerchief, my money. Diibil has no answer.
He admits he has been outwitted.
He leaves at dusk and never sees or hears of her again.

props.description: verseRibbon (planned effect, AN-103 and others): paper band 46 wide with squiggle lines unrolling along a keyed curve. This film adds: ink colour per speaker (blue Diibil, red lady, yellow edge Muslim), a row of metre marks (pattern A long long short long; pattern B short short long short; long = 26 x 6 stroke, short = 8 x 6), shape 'zigzag' (5 folds, 60 high), edge 'saw' (teeth 10 high) for the angry verses, curl '?' at the tip, one loop of radius 70 round a head, icons moonEye, tears, sun, wipe, heart, thorn, smirk (each about 34 px).

Silk kerchief, 90 x 90 when flat: yellow with a red border 8 wide, a small star in each corner, four tassels 14 long. States: folded (40 x 26 pad), held (hangs from one corner as a diamond 90 wide, 120 long, lower corner sways with swing()), flat on a counter (parallelogram, skew 20), icon (40 px).
Planned coinPile: five single gold coins (r 12) that slide across the counter and sit in a palm; also the 40 px coin icon on the tags.

Planned foodTray (brass tray 150 x 16 with bread, dates, fruit) with the planned waterJug (60 x 110) standing on it; carried as one stack at chest height; ghost (dashed) state for the empty table at 84.92.

The private room door: townDoor(ctx, 740, 880, 540, 900, open, {arch: true, paint: red}) on the right of the room, dark inside. Adds a peephole: barred opening 70 x 50 centred about (810, 725) with three vertical bars and a sliding shutter (open 0..1); behind it the scene draws Muslim's eyes, brows and turban edge (person clipped to the opening).

subtitles.ar: كان الشاعر دعبل الخزاعي جالسًا عند باب في بغداد|حين مرت أمامه امرأة جميلة فلفتت نظره.|وقف يخاطبها ببيت من الشعر يصف فيه سهره ودموعه،|منتظرًا أن يسمع جوابها.
subtitles.en: The poet Diibil sat near a gate in Baghdad|when a beautiful woman passed.|He addressed her with a verse|about sleeplessness and tears.

subtitles.ar: لم تتجاهله المرأة، بل أجابت فورًا ببيت آخر له وزن ومعنى مناسب.|تعجب من سرعة بديهتها،|فنظم سؤالًا جديدًا عن الحب،|وردت هي بكلمات ذكية تظهر مهارتها في الشعر.
subtitles.en: She immediately answered in matching verse.|Amazed by her quick wit,|he tried another poetic question,|and she replied just as skillfully.

subtitles.ar: غيّر دعبل وزن شعره ليختبر معرفتها،|فغيرت المرأة جوابها من غير تردد.|ازداد إعجابه بها، وطلب أن ترافقه برضاها. وافقت وسارت معه،|لكنه لم يجد في بيته مكانًا يليق باستقبالها.
subtitles.en: Diibil changed the rhythm to test her,|but she matched it effortlessly.|With her consent she accompanied him,|although he had no suitable place to host her.

subtitles.ar: تذكر صديقه الشاعر مسلم بن الوليد،|الذي كان يملك بيتًا حسنًا.|قصداه، فرحب مسلم بهما ودعاهما إلى الدخول،|لكنه لم يكن يملك مالًا كافيًا لإعداد الطعام الذي يحتاجه الضيفان.
subtitles.en: He took her to his friend Muslim ibn al-Walid,|who owned a pleasant house.|Muslim welcomed them|but lacked money for refreshments.

subtitles.ar: أعطى مسلم دعبل منديلًا ثمينًا|ليبيعه في السوق ويشتري بثمنه ما يلزم.|خرج دعبل مسرعًا، وباع المنديل، واشترى الطعام والشراب،|ثم عاد وهو يظن أن صديقه ينتظره شاكرًا.
subtitles.en: Muslim gave Diibil a valuable kerchief|to sell.|Diibil bought food and drink with the proceeds|and returned expecting gratitude.

subtitles.ar: لكنه وجد أن مسلمًا أخذ المرأة إلى غرفة خاصة وأغلق الباب.|تناول منه ما اشتراه وشكره بكلمات ساخرة،|ثم تركه واقفًا في الخارج. فهم دعبل أن صديقه قد استغل غيابه.
subtitles.en: Instead, Muslim had taken the woman into a private room.|He accepted the purchases, mockingly thanked Diibil|and shut the door in his face.

subtitles.ar: تبادل الشاعران أبياتًا لاذعة من خلف الباب، واشتد غضب دعبل.|أجابه مسلم بأنه هو صاحب البيت والمنديل والمال،|وسأله كيف يلومه بعدما أنفق من ماله واستضافهما في داره.
subtitles.en: The two poets traded sharp verses.|Muslim reminded Diibil that the house, kerchief and money|had all belonged to him.

subtitles.ar: أدرك دعبل في النهاية أنه خسر الفرصة والمال الذي تعب في إنفاقه، وأن صديقه غلبه بالحيلة.|ترك الباب منصرفًا بحسرة،|ويقول الراوي إنه لم ير المرأة بعد ذلك ولم يسمع عنها خبرًا.
subtitles.en: Diibil finally admitted he had been outwitted.|He left in frustration|and, the narrator says, never saw or heard of the woman again.

new_assets.name: verseRibbon
new_assets.description: Planned poetry ribbon (AN-103, AN-124 to AN-127) extended with metre marks, zigzag shape, saw edge, question curl, head loop and ink colour. The film's main device: verse, metre and matching are seen, not read.
new_assets.implementation: One function verseRibbon(ctx, pts, {len, w: 46, ink, metre, shape, edge, curl, icons}). Sample the keyed polyline (or bezier) by arc length up to len; offset by the normal for the two edges; fill paper, stroke black 5; squiggle lines as sine strokes in the ink colour; metre marks as rounded bars spaced 44 apart along the centre line; zigzag = replace the path by 5 alternating 60 high folds; saw edge = triangle teeth on the upper edge; loop = insert a circle of r 70 at a given point, drawn in back and front halves; scroll curl at the leading end as a 1.5 turn spiral of r 14.

new_assets.name: person costume preset 'poet'
new_assets.description: Planned preset (AN-103): green robe, yellow sash, small tilted white turban with a hanging tail, short pointed black beard, quill. This film uses the tail as secondary motion (tail lag field: angle in radians).
new_assets.implementation: Add to COSTUME in cast/people.js as a villager variant; tail is a 50 x 14 tapered band hinged at the turban side, angle from P.tail (default 0) so scenes can drive it with swing() or a 3 frame lag of the head velocity.

new_assets.name: kerchief
new_assets.description: Embroidered silk kerchief with folded, held, flat and icon states (sizes under props).
new_assets.implementation: Polygon of 4 corners with a red inner border, star() in each corner, tassels as short lines; held state hangs the polygon from one corner and rotates it with swing(); unfurl scales from the fold pad with overshoot.

new_assets.name: peephole (townDoor option)
new_assets.description: Barred peephole with sliding shutter in a door leaf so a character behind a closed door can still act with eyes and brows.
new_assets.implementation: In the scene: after townDoor, clip a 70 x 50 rounded rect, fill dark, draw the person behind it (same clip), then 3 bars 6 wide and a shutter rect that slides by open; black brush outline. Could later become townDoor option peep.

owner_questions: SCRIPT: the English is a shorter summary than the Arabic in P1 (omits "waiting to hear her answer"), P6 (omits "Diibil understood his friend had used his absence"), P7 (omits "and asked how he could blame him...") and P8 (omits the lost chance and money); both are kept verbatim, with fewer English chunks where needed.
The private room is staged discreetly: only a closing door, a sleeve and a robe hem are seen and nothing inside is ever shown (default: keep it this implicit).
The lady is shown going with Muslim of her own accord and is never shown distressed; the script does not say how she felt (default: neutral, her face is not seen at that moment).

Muslim is shown planning the trick from the moment he sees the lady (a lingering look at 77.28, darting eyes at 87.74, a wink at 96.36); the script only says Diibil later understood it (default: keep the visible plan for dramatic irony).

Invented comic business beyond the script: the mouse in Diibil's room, the moth from the empty purse, the kick at the door and hurt foot, the peephole in the door, and the final tip of the turban (default: keep all).

Invented lettering: MATCH!, QUICK WIT!, 3 FOR 3!, NO MONEY, VALUABLE!, SOLD!, THANK YOU!, PRIVATE ROOM, SLAM!, THANKS, FRIEND!, TRICKED!, HIS HOUSE, HIS KERCHIEF, HIS MONEY, HA HA! and the card MEANWHILE... (default: keep; 19 items with the two name labels, BAGHDAD and THE END).
Names on screen are spelled DIIBIL and MUSLIM as in the English script (default: keep those spellings).
implementation_notes: Cue everything from timing.json with w(p, n); the times in this plan are the word starts from timeline.md. Film length 179.87 s (175.87 + 4.0 hold), under the 180 s limit: do not lengthen the hold.

Verses are never written out. A verse = one verseRibbon; metre = the row of long and short marks; a match = the two rows lining up and flashing. Keep ribbons in the band y 540..680, above the heads, and never across a face.
The street is one baked 2400 strip; move with camX (ctx.translate(-camX, 0)). Read door, stall and palace anchors from the value marketStreet returns instead of the approximate x values here.

Person figures are front-facing: a "turn" is eyes first (gazePlan), then tip toward the target 0.2 s later. Walks use walk(xf, t, {stride}) with footfalls so feet never slide; the run at 96.92 uses stride 110 and tip 0.14.
Set LIFE.t = t each frame for auto-blinks; suppress blinks (noBlink) during the held looks at 17.8, 124.88 and 127.6.
Mask on / mask off for Muslim: the smooth or sly face appears only when Diibil's eyes are elsewhere (77.28, 81.6 to 84.2, 87.74, 96.36); when Diibil looks at him he is the warm host.

Partial figures at the inner door (hem at 113.74, sleeve at 114.74, arm at 118.22, head at 120.74) are the normal person drawn inside a clip of the door opening (evenodd clip as in the Fox head-into-hole), with the door leaf drawn after.
Setup and payoff: the cupEar pose at 19.1 is repeated exactly at 173.28; the thought cloud of thanks at 105.8 uses the same room layout as the real empty room at 111.48.

Sound: the narration has only three real pauses, so only four effects: pop 10.7, chime 20.95, pop 42.3, chime 176.05 (and nothing on the slam, which lands on a word; it is carried by panel-only shake and lettering). SND master 0.6.

Counters: VERSES MATCHED 1, 2, 3 (29.28, 39.94, 50.54) top centre; coin counter 5 then down to 0 (100.6 to 102.4); score MUSLIM 3, DIIBIL 0 built at 144.24, 144.84, 145.88. Use S.counter; hide each when its scene ends.
Subtitles: P6, P7 and P8 use 3 chunks because the English is shorter; chunk times follow the Arabic words.
Panel-only shake (template) for 117.12 and 139.12; the caption panel never moves.
warnings: Dense narration: no room for sound effects at the door slam, the kick or the market; do not add effects over words.
